original_value: AbstractWe propose a new FHE scheme F-NTRU that adopts the flattening technique proposed in GSW to derive an NTRU based scheme that (similar to GSW) does not require evaluation keys or key switching. Our scheme eliminates the decision small polynomial ratio assumption but relies only on the standard R-LWE assumption. It uses wide key distributions, and hence is immune to Subfield Lattice Attack. In practice, our scheme achieves competitive timings compared to the existing schemes. We are able to compute a homomorphic multiplication in 24.4 msec and 76.0 msec for 5 and 30 levels, respectively, without amortization. Furthermore, our scheme features small ciphertexts, e.g. 2376 KB for 30 levels. The assurance gained by using wide key distributions along with the message space flexibility of the scheme, i.e. bits, binary polynomials, and integers with a large message space, allows the use of the proposed scheme in a wide array of applications.

result.paraphrase: Abstract: We present F-NTRU, a new FHE scheme that uses the flattening technique from GSW to construct an NTRU-based system which, like GSW, needs neither evaluation keys nor key switching. The scheme removes the decision small polynomial ratio assumption and depends only on the standard R-LWE assumption. Because it uses wide key distributions, it is resistant to Subfield Lattice Attack. In practice, it delivers competitive runtimes versus existing schemes: without amortization, homomorphic multiplication takes 24.4 msec for 5 levels and 76.0 msec for 30 levels. It also provides compact ciphertexts, for example 2376 KB at 30 levels. The security from wide key distributions, together with flexible message spaces—bits, binary polynomials, and integers with a large message space—makes the scheme suitable for a broad range of applications.
